message.content:
You are reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary as a BLACK BOX. The binary is at /workspace/dataset/test15_executable.

Invocation contract: it takes EXACTLY 6 positional args: scheme host port path query fragment.
It prints 8 lines to stdout: scheme(), host(), port(), path(), query(), fragment(), to_string(), is_valid().

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT:
- You may ONLY run the binary and observe stdout/stderr/exit code. There is NO C++ source available; do not look for any.
- ALWAYS quote every argument in the shell, including empty ones: /workspace/dataset/test15_executable "http" "example.com" "80" "/" "" ""
- Make output unambiguous. Use a helper that numbers the lines and marks empties, e.g.:
    p(){ printf '### IN: [%s]\n' "$*"; /workspace/dataset/test15_executable "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; printf '  exit=%d\n' $?; nl -ba -s': ' /tmp/o | sed 's/$/<END>/'; if [ -s /tmp/e ]; then echo "  STDERR: $(cat /tmp/e)"; fi; }
  Then call p with 6 quoted args. Beware: trailing empty args are easy to lose — verify your helper really passes 6.
- Run MANY cases (30+ minimum). Batch them into a few Bash calls; do not do one call per case.
- Be exhaustive about the boundary cases in your assigned dimension.
- Do not guess. Every rule you report must be backed by an observed input/output pair you actually ran.

Baseline facts already established (re-verify if relevant to you):
- ("http","example.com","80","/","","")  -> lines: http / example.com / 80 / "/" / "" / "" / "http://example.com:80/" / 1
- ("http","example.com","-1","/","","") -> to_string is "http://example.com/"  (port omitted), port() prints -1
- ("http","example.com","0","/","","")  -> to_string is "http://example.com:0/"  (port 0 IS included)
- ("http","","80","/","","")            -> to_string is "http://:80/", is_valid=1
- ("","example.com","80","/","","")     -> to_string is "/" (scheme+authority both vanish), is_valid=1
- ("","","0","","","")                  -> to_string is "", is_valid=0

Report rules as precise, implementable statements (pseudocode-level), each with the concrete evidence line.


DIMENSION: what from_components does to the path string (line 4 = path()) and how it lands in to_string().

- Empty path "" with scheme+host set: is it stored as "" or defaulted to "/"?
- No leading slash: "foo", "foo/bar".
- Trailing slash: "/foo/", "/".
- Dot segments: "/a/./b", "/a/../b", "/../a", "/a/b/..", "/a/b/../..", "/./", "//a//b//", "///".
  IMPORTANT: determine whether from_components applies normalize_path() automatically or stores verbatim.
- Whitespace: " /a", "/a ", "/a b", tab/newline inside.
- Percent-encodings: "/a%20b", "/a%2Fb", "/%zz", "/a+b" -> decoded? encoded? verbatim?
- Special chars: "/a?b", "/a#b" (does an embedded ? or # get split into query/fragment?), "/a;b", "/a&b".
- UTF-8 multibyte path, 500-char path.
Report which are verbatim vs transformed, with evidence.

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text: All verbatim at the byte level. I have ~65 observed cases; compiling results.

input.dimension: path handling in from_components: what happens to the path string (line 4 = path()) and how it lands in to_string()

rules.rule: Empty path is stored VERBATIM as the empty string. It is NOT defaulted/normalized to "/", even when both scheme and host are set. path() prints an empty line.
rules.evidence: ("http","example.com","80","","","") -> line4=""<END>, line7="http://example.com:80"<END>, line8=1. Compare ("http","example.com","80","/","","") -> line4="/", line7="http://example.com:80/"

rules.rule: If path is non-empty and its FIRST BYTE is not '/', exactly one '/' is prepended. This happens at construction time (it is visible in path(), line 4), not only in to_string(). Pseudocode: if (!path.empty() && path[0] != '/') path = "/" + path;

The leading-slash insertion is unconditional on the first byte: it fires for ANY non-'/' first character, including space, TAB, CR, '.', '?', '#', '\\', and a letter followed by ':' (no scheme-relative or query/fragment special-casing).
The leading-slash insertion ignores scheme and host entirely — it applies with empty host, empty scheme, and non-hierarchical schemes, producing triple slashes in to_string().
rules.evidence: ("http","","-1","foo","","") -> line4="/foo", line7="http:///foo". ("mailto","","-1","user@example.com","","") -> line4="/user@example.com", line7="mailto:///user@example.com". ("","","-1","foo","","") -> line4="/foo", line7="/foo"

rules.rule: A path already starting with '/' is stored byte-for-byte unchanged: no second slash added, no duplicate-slash collapsing, no trailing-slash addition or removal.
from_components does NOT apply normalize_path(). Dot segments ('.', '..') are stored completely verbatim — never resolved, collapsed, or removed, in any position (leading, middle, trailing).
Relative dot inputs get only the slash prefix, no resolution: "." -> "/.", ".." -> "/..", "././" -> "/././".
Segments that merely look dot-like are untouched (no over-eager matching): "/...." and "/a/..b/c" pass through.
No whitespace trimming or stripping anywhere in the path. Leading, trailing and interior spaces, TABs, CRs, LFs are preserved byte-for-byte.
rules.evidence:
"/a " -> line4="/a "; "/a b" -> "/a b"; " " -> line4="/ ", line7="http://example.com:80/ "; "/a	b" -> "/a	b"; od of ("http","h","80","/ab") = `/ a  b 
` on line 4 and `... : 8 0 / a  b` in to_string; od of "/a
b" shows literal `
` inside the stored path (so the 8 logical fields print as 10 physical lines)

rules.rule: No percent-decoding. %XX escapes are stored verbatim, including %2F (which is NOT decoded to '/'), %20, %41, %00.

No percent-ENCODING either: unsafe characters are never escaped on the way in or out. Space stays a raw space, '\\', '[', ']', DEL (0x7F) and even the invalid-UTF-8 byte 0xFF survive unchanged in both path() and to_string().
rules.evidence: "/a b" -> "/a b" (not "/a%20b"); "/a\\b" -> "/a\\b"; "/a[b]" -> "/a[b]"; od of "/a\177b" -> line4 bytes `/ a 177 b`; od of "/a\377b" -> line4 bytes `/ a 377 b`, exit=0

rules.rule: Malformed percent escapes are accepted and stored verbatim with no validation, error, or effect on is_valid().
'+' in the path is NOT converted to space (and space is not converted to '+').
No splitting on embedded '?' or '#': from_components never re-parses the path, so an embedded query/fragment delimiter stays inside path() and query()/fragment() stay empty.
rules.evidence: "/a?b" -> line4="/a?b", line5="", line6="", line7="http://example.com:80/a?b"; "/a#b" -> line4="/a#b", line5="", line6=""; "/a?b#c" -> line4="/a?b#c", line5="", line6="", line7="http://example.com:80/a?b#c"

rules.rule: Other sub-delims and reserved characters (';', '&', '=', '@', ':') are stored verbatim with no interpretation.
No case folding of the path. (Contrast: scheme IS lowercased, host is not, path is not.)
UTF-8 multibyte sequences pass through unchanged (no IDNA/punycode/percent-encoding of non-ASCII).
rules.evidence: "/héllo/日本" -> line4="/héllo/日本", line7="http://example.com:80/héllo/日本"; "/…/ünicode%C3%A9" -> line4="/…/ünicode%C3%A9"

rules.rule: No length cap or truncation on the path.
rules.evidence: path = "/" + 5000 'c' chars -> line4 length = 5001, line7 length = 5022 (= len("http://example.com:80")=21 + 5001), line8=1, exit=0. A 500-'b' relative path -> line4 = "/" + 500 b's

rules.rule: to_string() splices the STORED path in verbatim with no separator of its own, and synthesizes NO '/' when the path is empty — so an empty path with a query yields "host:port?query" (authority immediately followed by '?'). Layout: to_string = (scheme.empty() ? "" : scheme + "://" + host + (port >= 0 ? ":" + itoa(port) : "")) + path + (query.empty() ? "" : "?" + query) + (fragment.empty() ? "" : "#" + fragment)

When scheme is empty, to_string() drops the whole "scheme://host[:port]" prefix and the path becomes the start of the string (a path-only relative reference); the stored slash-prefix is what makes it start with '/'.
rules.evidence: ("","example.com","80","/foo","","") -> line2="example.com", line3="80", line4="/foo", line7="/foo"; ("","example.com","-1","foo","","") -> line4="/foo", line7="/foo"; ("","","-1","//foo","","") -> line7="//foo"; ("","example.com","80","","","") -> line7="" (empty)

rules.rule: is_valid() is driven by emptiness of host and path only: is_valid == (!host.empty() || !path.empty()). Scheme, query and fragment do not make it valid. Because any non-empty path input is slash-prefixed and thus non-empty, supplying ANY non-empty path makes the URL valid even with empty scheme and host.

Path content never affects is_valid(): every syntactically hostile path tested (spaces, control bytes, 0xFF, bad escapes, embedded ?/#, dot segments) still yielded is_valid()=1 and exit=0. Only emptiness matters.
Exit code is always 0 and stderr always empty regardless of path content (including invalid UTF-8 and 5000-char paths); malformed paths are never rejected via process status.
rules.evidence: All ~65 runs reported exit=0 with no STDERR line, including od runs on "/a\377b" (exit=0) and the 5000-char run (exit=0, /tmp/e5 empty)

rawObservations: (http, example.com, 80, '/a<LF>b', , ) -> path contains literal LF; output shows 10 physical lines
(http, h, 80, /a<CR>b, , ) via od -> line4 bytes '/ a \r b', to_string bytes '...:80/a\rb', valid=1
(http, h, 80, /a<LF>b, , ) via od -> line4 bytes '/ a \n b'
(http, h, 80, /a<0x7F>b, , ) via od -> line4 bytes '/ a 177 b'
(http, h, 80, ' /a', , ) via od -> line4 bytes '/ <sp> / a'
(http, h, 80, /a<0xFF>b, , ) via od -> line4 bytes '/ a 377 b', exit=0
(http, example.com, 80, /+5000c, , ) -> line4 len=5001, line7 len=5022, valid=1, exit=0
uncertainties: A NUL byte inside the path cannot be tested through argv, so behavior on embedded '\0' is unknown.

I could not distinguish whether the '/' prefix is added inside from_components or inside a path setter it calls — only that it is observable in path() (line 4), i.e. it is stored, not applied lazily in to_string().
Whether the class exposes a separate normalize_path() that could be called explicitly is not observable from this 8-line output; the only established fact is that from_components does NOT normalize.
Paths beyond 5000 chars (e.g. >1 MB, or near ARG_MAX) were not tested, so I cannot rule out a very large cap.

is_valid() appears to be exactly (!host.empty() || !path.empty()), but I only sampled schemes 'http', 'mailto', 'x' and empty; a pathological scheme might add another validity term that interacts with path.
Because the slash prefix guarantees any non-empty input path is stored non-empty, I could not construct a case with non-empty input path but empty stored path to further isolate the is_valid() term.
